answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring every new identity to lock a ferrous bond equal to 0.1% of the current atlas of total locked value, held for a 12-epoch horizon. The bond is fully slashed if a peer-attested audit detects shared operator keys. The Nth fake forces the attacker to lock an ever-larger ferrous stake that scales with network growth, while the multi-epoch horizon blocks rapid recycling. Parallel farms pay linear capital per head plus opportunity cost, making bulk sybil creation unprofitable beyond a few identities.
